--- file: capsule/waits_parse.py ---
--- head ---
"""A card/comment/branch marker's own `waits: <token>` line (row 529, decision row 529):
recognised only as a line-start key, the exact same shape `capsule.cardmeta.parse_builds`
uses for `builds:` - never matched mid-sentence. Its own module (mirroring `cardmeta.py`'s
own reason for existing) so the parser can be tested apart from `unblocked.py`, which is
frozen at its row-514 size baseline and has no room left to hold this regex itself.

Row 519/529: a card's own triage-log line, such as "triage 2026-09-28 (row 519): KEEP,
the owner. Waits: the current landing queue; dispatch in priority order.", has "waits:"
mid-sentence - after "KEEP, the owner. " - not at that line's own start, so it must never be
read as a `waits: owner` marker. A prior, looser reading of this text hid 13 ready cards
as blocked on the owner (found 2026-09-29)."""
import re

WAITS_RE = re.compile(r"(?im)^\s*waits:\s*(.+?)\s*$")


def parse_waits(text):
    """`text`'s last `waits:` line's value (its last match wins - the freshest line, same
    "last match wins" shape as `cardmeta.parse_builds`); `None` when there is no such line.
    Recognised only as a line-start key: leading whitespace before `waits:` is allowed
    (indented under a bullet), anything else before it on the same physical line is not."""
    if not text:
        return None
    matches = WAITS_RE.findall(text)
    return matches[-1] if matches else None

import fnmatch

import shutil
import sqlite3

import time
from pathlib import Path
from capsule import cardmeta, config, dispatch, dispatch_gate, paths, spool


def parse_waits(text):
    """The `waits:` value in `text` (its last match wins - the freshest line), or None."""
    if not text:
        return None
    matches = WAITS_RE.findall(text)
    return matches[-1] if matches else None

--- head ---
import fnmatch
import glob
import json
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path
from capsule import cardmeta, config, dispatch, dispatch_gate, paths, spool, waits_parse


def parse_waits(text):
    """The `waits:` value in `text` (its last match wins - the freshest line), or None.
    This module is frozen at its row-514 size baseline, so the line-start-only regex
    itself (row 529) lives in its own module, `waits_parse.parse_waits`."""
    return waits_parse.parse_waits(text)
